existing.description_long: On January 21, 2025, Trump's executive order revoking EO 11246 triggered an immediate halt to all affirmative action enforcement for federal contractors, a 60-year-old framework protecting millions of workers. The Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP), housed within the Department of Labor, was ordered to immediately cease and desist all investigative and enforcement activity tied to EO 11246. Acting Labor Secretary Vincent Micone issued a memo on January 24 directing the agency accordingly, administratively closing all approximately 2,000 pending compliance reviews that the Biden administration had scheduled for fiscal year 2025. Companies including Meta, Google, and Pfizer that had been slated for civil rights audits received formal closure notices. The Obama-era EO 13672 — which specifically prohibited federal contractors from discriminating on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity — was also revoked, eliminating protection for LGBTQ+ workers at companies doing business with the federal government, estimated to involve roughly 25 percent of the U.S. civilian workforce. Federal contractors were given a 90-day grace period until April 21, 2025 to wind down compliance with the old regulatory scheme. New contracts and grants were required to include certifications that recipients do not run DEI programs deemed discriminatory. Civil rights advocates called it the most significant rollback of workforce civil rights protections since the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
